semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The 'xlm-r-base' is a variant of 'xlm-roberta', which is the central model that 'xlm-r-base' belongs to, therefore they are essentially the same model but with different configurations.

parent_models.justification: 'XLM-R', short for XLM-RoBERTa, is a transformer-based model, and 'xlm-r-base' is a specific configuration of this central model.

closest_parent_model.justification: 'XLM-RoBERTa' is the central model, with 'xlm-r-base' being one of its configuration options, making it the closest parent model.

child_models.justification: 'xlm-r-large' is another configuration under 'xlm-roberta', similar in style to 'xlm-r-base' but larger, thus making it a specific variant and considered a child model.

closest_child_model.justification: Among the listed models, 'xlm-r-large' represents another configuration of 'xlm-roberta', making it the closest child model of 'xlm-r-base'.

sibling_models.justification: 'xlm-r-large' is another variant/configuration of the 'xlm-roberta' model, making it a sibling to 'xlm-r-base'.

closest_sibling_model.justification: 'xlm-r-large' is another variant of the 'xlm-roberta' model, closely related to 'xlm-r-base', making it the closest sibling model.

unrelated_models.justification: 'lstm-am' is unrelated because it is an LSTM-based model, not a transformer.
'lstm' is unrelated as it represents a Long Short-Term Memory model, differing fundamentally in architecture.
'gpt-xl' is a variant of the GPT model and not directly related to 'xlm-r-base' or XLM-RoBERTa.
'gpt2-xlarge' is an expanded version of GPT-2, bearing no direct relevance to the XLM-R model family.
'deit-base' is related to vision tasks, using transformers differently than the 'xlm-r-base' for NLP.
'rbm' represents a different model architecture entirely, focused on Restricted Boltzmann Machines.
